question: The revenue from selling $x$ items is $R(x)=80x-x^2$ rupees, while the production cost is $C(x)=20x+100$ rupees. Find the number of items that maximises the profit and calculate the maximum profit.
explanation:
Profit function
Profit equals revenue minus cost:
$$P(x)=R(x)-C(x)$$
$$P(x)=80x-x^2-(20x+100)$$
$$P(x)=-x^2+60x-100$$
Stationary condition
$$P'(x)=-2x+60$$
Setting $P'(x)=0$ gives $x=30$.
Maximum verification
$$P''(x)=-2<0$$
Therefore, the profit is maximum at $x=30$.
Maximum profit
$$P(30)=-(30)^2+60(30)-100$$
$$=-900+1800-100=800$$
Conclusion
The profit is maximum when $30$ items are sold, and the maximum profit is ₹$800$.
